summary: This visual presents three related charts analyzing payroll and losses over the years 1998 to 2007. The first chart, titled 'Payroll ($M)', shows payroll values in millions, with the following data points: 1998 ($1.8M), 1999 ($2.0M), 2003 ($1.5M), 2004 ($1.6M), 2005 ($1.7M), 2006 ($2.1M), and 2007 ($2.3M). The second chart, 'Losses ($000)', illustrates losses in thousands, with values of 1998 ($30K), 1999 ($32K), 2003 ($20K), 2004 ($15K), 2005 ($5K), 2006 ($2K), and 2007 ($1K). The final chart, 'Losses per $1,000 of Payroll', shows a declining trend in losses per thousand dollars of payroll, with values of 1998 ($18.20), 1999 ($14.20), 2003 ($3.90), 2004 ($0.30), 2005 ($0.00), 2006 ($0.70), and 2007 ($0.30). The overall trend indicates a decrease in losses relative to payroll over the years.
